slice: Deepening pass 8: individual race tests for the thinnest pre-2020 motocross models - Husqvarna TC 250, TC 125, FC 350, FC 250 and KTM 125/150 SX (knowledge push 2026-11)

records.statement: For 2018 the TC 250 got air-fork updates (new air seal, air piston and rebound spring in the air leg, a new damping piston and firmer mid-stroke compression), shock valving to match, radiator guards with dirt-escape holes, a carburettor angle changed from 12 to 7 degrees, and a map switch on the handlebar in place of the 2017 wire hidden under the tank. List price $7,999.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2018 Husqvarna TC250 race test

records.topic: TC 250 2018 dyno, weight and power feel
records.statement: On a magazine dyno the 2018 TC 250 made 47 hp at 8,200 rpm and weighed 214 lb, 5 lb less than a YZ250. It surges hard from low to mid and is abrupt off the throttle, with no real top-end past 8,200 rpm: shift there.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2018 Husqvarna TC250 race test

records.topic: TC 250 2018 tester fork and shock settings
records.statement: A magazine crew's 2018 TC 250 setup. Fork (AER 48): 144 psi (stock 147), compression 23 clicks out (stock 12), rebound 19 out (stock 12), legs at the second line. If it bottoms below 144 psi, raise the pressure or add 5 cc of oil. Shock (42 N/mm spring): race sag 107 mm (stock 110) with 30-40 mm of free sag, high-speed compression 1-1/4 turns out (stock 2), low-speed compression 8 clicks out (stock 15), rebound 14 out (stock 15).

source.name: Motocross Action - 2018 Husqvarna TC250 race test

records.statement: Tested jetting for the 2018 TC 250 (38 mm Mikuni TMX, 60:1 premix): 450 main (stock 440), 45 pilot (stock 42.5), 43-73 needle on the third clip, air screw 1/4 turn out (stock 1-1/2). Gearing: 14/49 in place of the stock 14/50; novices and vets may prefer one tooth more at the rear.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2018 Husqvarna TC250 race test

records.statement: On the 2018 TC 250: sprocket bolts loosen and spokes need constant checking; the fuel cap sticks; the fork's air-side bleeder strips easily; the fork air valve is hard to reach; tie-down hooks can crimp the front brake hose. For the abrupt power, use the bar map switch and turn the power-valve adjuster clockwise (it takes a square-drive tool). An aftermarket pipe and silencer added about 3 hp from 7,000 to 9,500 rpm.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2018 Husqvarna TC250 race test

records.statement: A second test of the 2018 TC 250 found smooth, linear power with little vibration that flattens early on top and rewards staying in the midrange, which suits hardpack and slippery tracks. Stock jetting was close enough to leave alone on 60:1 with 92 octane, apart from a slight rich spot just off idle. Testers ran 100-105 mm of sag, slowed rebound a couple of clicks at both ends and raised fork pressure a few psi for faster riders; the shock spring is soft for heavier riders. The rear brake pedal return spring has broken on these bikes, which leaves no rear brake, so check it.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - 2018 Husqvarna TC250

records.topic: FC 350 2019 dyno, weight and power feel
records.statement: On a magazine dyno the 2019 FC 350 made 53.30 hp at peak and 50.82 hp near 10,000 rpm, against 48.76 hp there for the 2018 engine. It weighed 222 lb. It is snappy off idle, calmer in the middle and surges past 8,000 rpm to a 13,400 rpm limiter, so it should not be short-shifted. Testers raced on map two.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2019 Husqvarna FC350 race test

records.topic: FC 350 2019 tester fork and shock settings
records.statement: A magazine crew's 2019 FC 350 setup. Fork (AER 48): 140 psi (stock 152), compression 25 clicks out (stock 15), rebound 17 out (stock 15), legs at the third line. Shock: 42 N/mm spring (45 N/mm for riders over 185 lb), race sag 105 mm (stock 110), high-speed compression 1-3/4 turns out (stock 2), low-speed compression 15 clicks out, rebound 10 out (stock 15). Gearing: a 51-tooth rear, some testers 52.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2019 Husqvarna FC350 race test

records.statement: On the 2019 FC 350: the airbox is restrictive (drill five 1-1/4 inch holes in the cover behind the filter); the muffler has a restrictor cone (a straight-through muffler, or a full aftermarket system for about 2 hp); the rear sprocket bolts do not seat fully and loosen (lap the tapers and keep checking); spokes still loosen despite new nipples; the fork guards only cover the front, so fork seals wear; and the new two-piece subframe is less supple than the old one. The diaphragm-spring clutch proved durable.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2019 Husqvarna FC350 race test

records.topic: FC 250 2019 dyno with the airbox cover on and off
records.statement: On a magazine dyno the 2019 FC 250 made 42.48 hp stock and just under 44 hp with the airbox cover removed. It weighed 219 lb and listed at $9,099. It has quicker pickup and more midrange than before but is still strongest at high rpm, revving to a 14,000 rpm limiter. Traction control only helped on hardpack, mud and slick corner exits. The 2019 muffler has no internal restrictors.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2019 Husqvarna FC250 race test

records.topic: FC 250 2019 tester fork and shock settings
records.statement: A magazine crew's 2019 FC 250 setup. Fork (AER 48): 136 psi (stock 149), compression 28 clicks out (stock 15), rebound 17 out (stock 15), legs at the third line. Shock: 42 N/mm spring (45 over 185 lb, 39 under 130 lb), race sag 105 mm, high-speed compression 2-3/4 turns out (stock 2), low-speed compression 15 clicks out, rebound 11 out (stock 15).

source.name: Motocross Action - 2019 Husqvarna FC250 race test

records.statement: Stock gearing on the 2019 FC 250 is 14/51 (3.643), which testers found tall. A 13-tooth countershaft gives 3.923 with the 51, 3.846 with a 50 and 3.769 with a 49. Check the rear sprocket bolts and spokes regularly; both loosen.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2019 Husqvarna FC250 race test

records.topic: FC 350 2016 weight, price and power feel
records.statement: The all-new 2016 FC 350 weighed 229 lb without fuel and listed at $9,199. The engine is 20 mm shorter and nearly 3 lb lighter than the 2015 one, and the chassis lost about 7 lb, much of it from a lithium battery. Peak power is in the low 50s. It builds strongly above 9,000 rpm, peaks near 12,000 and revs to 14,000, with less engine braking than a 450. It is electric start only, cold-blooded, and the clutch pull is firm.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine - Husqvarna FC350 full test

records.statement: On the 2016 FC 350 the 4CS fork takes big hits and holds the front up but is harsh over small, rapid bumps, and its compression clicker only changes big-hit behaviour, so a revalve is the cure. Most riders ran 105-110 mm of sag. The handling gets better the faster it is ridden. Against the 350 SX-F it differs in bodywork, muffler, clutch master cylinder, tyres and suspension settings.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine - Husqvarna FC350 full test

records.statement: The TC 125 was all new for 2016: a new engine (cylinder, piston, crankshaft and cases) about 2 kg lighter at 17.2 kg, a six-speed gearbox 200 g lighter with unchanged ratios, a new chromoly frame, a carbon-composite subframe 1 kg lighter at 1.4 kg, a revised 4CS fork, a new shock 12 mm shorter with 3 mm less stroke on 148.2 mm pull rods (145 before), and a Magura hydraulic clutch. Final drive is 13/50. The maker claims 38-40 hp. Fork clickers: white dial on the left for compression, red on the right for rebound.

source.name: Dirt Action - 2016 Husqvarna TC 125

records.statement: For 2012 the 150 SX changed from no-link PDS to the rising-rate linkage from the four-strokes, with a new shock, frame shock tower, one-piece cast swingarm and air boot. It also got a cylinder-head stay to cut vibration, new fork and shock seals, bushings and damping, and an exhaust retuned for midrange. It weighs about 205 lb, 5 lb more than 2011.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2012 KTM 150SX test

records.statement: On a magazine dyno the 2012 150 SX made 38.83 hp at 11,100 rpm, down from just over 40 hp in 2011. The powerband is narrow and suits gun-and-run riding; below 10,000 rpm a 250 four-stroke makes much more power.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2012 KTM 150SX test

records.topic: 150 SX 2012 tester suspension, jetting and gearing
records.statement: A magazine crew's 2012 150 SX setup. Fork: 0.42 kg/mm springs (0.44 for heavier or faster riders), 350 cc oil, compression 6 clicks out (stock 12), rebound 10 out (stock 12). Shock: 4.7 kg/mm spring, race sag 100 mm, high-speed compression 2 turns out, low-speed compression 15 clicks out, rebound 15 out; with free sag under 35 mm go to the next stiffer spring. Jetting: 185 main (stock 182), 40 pilot, NOZI needle on the second clip, air screw 1-1/2 turns; in cool weather a 190 main and 42 pilot. Gearing: a 51-tooth rear in place of the 50.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2012 KTM 150SX test

records.statement: On a magazine dyno the 2013 125 SX made 34.66 hp at 11,200 rpm and 16.41 lb-ft at 11,000 rpm: 14.90 hp at 7,000 rpm, 20.66 at 8,000, 25.37 at 9,000, 30.20 at 10,000, 34.37 at 11,000 and 29.20 at 12,000. It weighed 206.5 lb and listed at $6,449.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2013 KTM 125SX vs KTM 150SX

records.statement: On a magazine dyno the 2013 150 SX made 38.83 hp at 11,100 rpm and 18.46 lb-ft at 10,900 rpm: 17.45 hp at 7,000 rpm, 23.37 at 8,000, 29.07 at 9,000, 34.02 at 10,000, 38.83 at 11,000 and 32.97 at 12,000, about 3-4 hp more than the 125 SX everywhere. It weighed 207 lb.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2013 KTM 125SX vs KTM 150SX

records.topic: 125 SX against 150 SX (2013): mechanical differences and who each suits
records.statement: The 2013 125 SX is 124.8 cc (54 x 54.5 mm) and the 150 SX 143.6 cc (56 x 58.4 mm), with different crank, cylinder, piston, power valve and rings. The 150 has all-steel clutch drive plates with stiffer springs and a leaner pilot jet. Test riders rated the 125's handling and suspension better and its powerband more usable when ridden hard; vets preferred the 150's stronger pull, easier starts and jumping. The 125 suits riders moving up from an 85; the 150 suits older riders and practice days.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2013 KTM 125SX vs KTM 150SX

records.topic: 125 SX and 150 SX 2013 tester suspension, jetting and gearing
records.statement: A magazine crew's 2013 setup, shared by the 125 SX and 150 SX. Fork: 0.42 kg/mm springs (0.44 or more for heavier riders), 360 cc oil, compression 6 clicks out, rebound 10 out, legs 5 mm up. Shock: 4.8 kg/mm spring, race sag 100 mm, high-speed compression 2 turns out, low-speed compression 15 clicks out, rebound 15 out. Jetting (38 mm PWK): 185 main, 40 pilot, NOZI needle, air screw 1-1/2 turns, with the clip third from top on the 125 and second from top on the 150; for cold or soft conditions a 190 main and 42 pilot. Gearing: one tooth more at the rear, two for tight tracks.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2013 KTM 125SX vs KTM 150SX
